name: Codex Musica — boot index (the lazy app's first view: every genre without its prose, plus the starter genres'; internal — the published index is browse.json)

items.name: Delta blues
items.lineage: Country-blues tradition of the Mississippi Delta region — slide-guitar-and-vocal solo and small-ensemble repertoire developed in the early twentieth century through the lineage of Charley Patton (the 1929 Paramount recordings), Son House, Robert Johnson (the 1936-37 San Antonio and Dallas sessions), Skip James, Bukka White, and continuing through the post-WWII Chicago-blues electrification by Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, and others
items.description: Delta blues tradition (Mississippi cotton-belt, 1900-1940), the rural-acoustic precursor to electric Chicago blues. Solo male vocal-with-acoustic-guitar form: steel-bodied resonator or wooden flat-top, often played with bottleneck slide (glass or metal), sometimes alternating-bass thumb pattern. Free-meter vocals (12-bar blues frame loosely observed), characteristic minor-third-and-flatted-seventh blue-notes, single-chord modal vamps as foundation. Repertoire: Robert Johnson 1936-1937 recordings, Charley Patton, Son House, Skip James, Bukka White. Distinguished from Piedmont blues by single-chord-modal-not-ragtime-fingerpicking foundation; distinguished from later electric blues by acoustic-non-amplified form.

items.name: Late Romantic symphonic
items.lineage: Western orchestral classical music tradition spanning the Classical period (Haydn, Mozart symphonic forms ca. 1760-1800), Romantic period (Beethoven through Mahler, ca. 1800-1910), and twentieth-century continuation — characterized by the standardized symphony orchestra ensemble of strings-winds-brass-percussion, the multi-movement symphony, concerto, and tone-poem forms, and the conductor-led-large-ensemble performance model
items.description: Symphonic / orchestral classical (codified mid-18th century onward through pre-Classical and Classical-era symphonic development, with continuous tradition through Beethoven's mature symphonies, Romantic-and-late-Romantic continuation, 20th-century modernist and postmodernist works, and contemporary continuation through to present), the large-orchestra notated tradition. Defined by full-orchestra ensemble (typically 60-100+ musicians across string, woodwind, brass, percussion, and harp sections), through-composed sonata-form, theme-and-variations, fugal, and other classical compositional forms, full dynamic range from intimate-pianissimo soloistic passages to fortissimo-tutti climaxes, no improvisation in classical practice (every note specified in score), repertoire spanning Classical core canon (Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven), Romantic continuation (Brahms, Bruckner, Mahler), 20th-century modernist (Stravinsky, Bartók, Shostakovich), and contemporary new-music continuation, and concert-hall performance contexts with subscription-orchestra institutional framing. Distinguished from chamber music by ensemble size; distinguished from opera by absence of vocal-and-stage component (or, in operas, the orchestral-pit-foundation of opera); distinguished from band music by string-section foundation rather than wind-band.

items.name: Hindustani classical
items.lineage: North Indian classical raga tradition organized through the gharana (lineage-school) transmission system across Gwalior, Agra, Patiala, Kirana, Atrauli-Jaipur, Indore, Mewati, Benares gharanas — codified through V.N. Bhatkhandes 10-thaat system in the early 20th century, 20th-century lineage Ustad Bismillah Khan (shehnai), Ravi Shankar (sitar), Vilayat Khan (sitar), Ali Akbar Khan (sarod), Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Kirana vocal), Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (bansuri)
items.description: Hindustani classical music (codified 13th-15th century onward through Sufi-Hindu syncretic court traditions in Delhi, Lahore, Agra, and Lucknow, with the gharana family-disciple lineage system organizing transmission from 18th century onward), the North Indian classical tradition. The instrumental configuration is sitar lead, tabla rhythmic accompaniment, and tanpura drone-strings. Defined by raga-based modal melody (each raga a specific melodic-grammar with characteristic phrases, ascending-and-descending scales, and emotional-association), tanpura drone establishing the tonic and fifth as foundation, elaborate microtonal ornamentation (meend pitch-bending glides, gamak rapid oscillation, andolan slow vibrato, kan grace-note embellishment), and tabla percussion supplying the tala metric cycle (most commonly teental 16-beat, jhaptal 10-beat, ektal 12-beat). Other soloist instruments and vocal styles (sarod, bansuri, voice-led khayal, dhrupad, thumri) carry their own distinct sub-traditions in the codex. Distinguished from Carnatic by Persian-Sufi-and-Mughal influence, raga-elaboration-foreground over composition-foreground, and tabla-not-mridangam percussion; distinguished from Indian filmi by classical-not-pop framing.

items.name: Detroit techno
items.lineage: Mid-1980s Detroit electronic dance music genre developed by the Belleville Three (Juan Atkins, Derrick May, Kevin Saunderson) drawing on Kraftwerk's electronic vocabulary, Parliament-Funkadelic's Afrofuturist aesthetic, and Chicago house's rhythmic foundation — codified through Cybotron (Clear 1983), Model 500, Rhythim Is Rhythim (Strings of Life 1987), Inner City (Big Fun 1988), and the labels Metroplex, Transmat, KMS
items.description: Detroit techno (codified 1985-1990 through the Belleville Three — Juan Atkins, Derrick May, Kevin Saunderson — and the Cybotron precursor work, with second-wave Underground Resistance lineage 1990 onward), the Detroit-originated mechanical-funk electronic music genre. Defined by drum-machine four-on-floor foundation (TR-909 kicks, TR-808 hats and claps, TR-606 snares), synthesizer-derived bass lines and lead lines drawing from Kraftwerk-Yellow-Magic-Orchestra futurist palette, atmospheric synth-pad layers and processed sound effects, song-form built on long sectional vamps for DJ-mixing, futurist-sci-fi lyrical content (when vocals appear), and tempos around 125-140 BPM. Production lineage emerging from black Detroit producers' response to disco's death and Reagan-era Rust-Belt deindustrialization. Distinguished from Chicago house by mechanical-not-soulful aesthetic and futurist-not-disco lineage; distinguished from European techno by warmer Detroit funk-and-soul traces; distinguished from acid house by absence of TB-303-foreground.

items.name: Dub
items.lineage: Jamaican instrumental remix-and-effects genre invented by King Tubby (Osbourne Ruddock) in the late 1960s through the early 1970s in his Waterhouse-district Kingston home workshop — created by taking the rhythm tracks (riddims) of existing reggae recordings and live-re-mixing them through tape delay (Roland Space Echo), spring reverb, and dropout-mute manipulation; codified through King Tubby, Lee Scratch Perry (his Black Ark studio canon), Augustus Pablo (King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown 1976), Scientist (Hopeton Brown, Tubbys protégé)
items.description: Dub (codified 1968-1975 Jamaica through King Tubby, Lee Scratch Perry, and Errol Thompson establishing the genre's mixing-board-as-instrument approach), the Jamaican production-aesthetic-as-genre that emerged from reggae instrumentals reworked at the mixing console. Defined by reggae-instrumental foundation (the dub track is typically built from the existing reggae multitrack rather than recorded fresh), heavy spring-reverb-and-tape-delay processing of individual elements (vocal, snare, guitar chops processed with extreme delay-and-reverb feed-back), dropping-vocal-in-and-out technique (vocal track muted-and-unmuted across the song to highlight the rhythm-section), bass-and-drums-foreground mixing (the riddim section pushed up while melodic elements get periodically removed), and live-mix performance aesthetic where the engineer's real-time mixing-console manipulation IS the performance. Distinguished from straight reggae by mixing-board-foreground-as-genre and absence of fixed-vocal-arrangement; distinguished from later dub-techno by Jamaican-not-Berlin/Cologne lineage and reggae-rhythm foundation; distinguished from later dancehall by analog-mixing-board production over digital-riddim foundation.

items.name: Southern soul (Stax / FAME / Muscle Shoals tradition)
Javanese gamelan
items.lineage: Javanese bronze-percussion court-and-village tradition tuned in slendro five-tone-and-pelog seven-tone systems, with two parallel lineages: the kraton-court refined-style of Yogyakarta and Surakarta (16th-century onward, Mataram successor sultanates) and the village kemasan rural-ensemble style. The full court gamelan comprises 30-to-40 instruments organized into balungan core-melody bonang-saron, panerusan elaborating-melody gender-rebab-suling, and gong-kempul colotomic-structural-time-markers, performed cyclically through gendhing pieces of nested 8-16-32-64-128 beat irama tempo-density levels. The wayang shadow-puppet performance is the canonical embedding context, where gamelan accompanies dalang puppeteer-narration through pathet modal sections aligned to night-narrative time.
items.description: Javanese gamelan (codified continuously from at least 9th century Javanese court contexts through to present, with central-Javanese karaton (court) gamelan of Yogyakarta and Surakarta as the codifying-classical lineage), the Javanese bronze-metallophone ensemble tradition. Defined by sléndro (5-tone) and pélog (7-tone) tuning systems each with distinct emotional-and-occasion association, cyclical colotomic structure where punctuating gongs of various sizes mark the cycle's metric divisions (gong ageng marking the longest cycle, kenong-kempul-kethuk subdividing within), interlocking instrumental textures with multiple metallophones playing complementary phrases at different rhythmic densities, dance-and-shadow-puppet wayang-kulit performance contexts, and sindhen female solo vocal and gérong male chorus singing on top of the instrumental texture. Distinguished from Balinese gamelan by slower tempos, absence of paired-tuning shimmer, and tuning-flexibility within a single performance; distinguished from Sundanese gamelan by central-Javanese lineage and karaton classical context.
